subject: E-Commerce
title: Temu vs Amazon: The Price War
description: A 60-second lesson on Temu vs Amazon: The Price War.

hook.text: Temu's average item costs $8. Amazon's costs $25. Temu attacks from the bottom with prices Amazon can't match.

buildup.text: Temu connects Chinese factories to US consumers, eliminating warehouses, middlemen, and markup layers.

discovery.text: Temu spends $30+ to acquire each customer through ads. It's burning billions to build habit and market share.

twist.text: Amazon responded by launching 'Amazon Haul'—discount items under $20 shipped directly from China. The war is now direct.

climax.text: Price wars benefit consumers short-term but destroy margins for everyone. Someone eventually runs out of money.

punchline.text: $8 vs $25 average. Temu attacks from below; Amazon launches its own discount.

quiz.question: How is Temu able to offer such low prices?
options: Direct factory-to-consumer model that eliminates middlemen and warehousing costs
